items.name: RFA Checklist Extraction
items.description: Uploads a federal funding announcement (RFA, FOA, NOFO, or program solicitation) and returns a single RA-friendly Markdown checklist organized in the eight pre-award sections a sponsored-programs analyst uses when triaging an opportunity: Dates & Deadlines, Eligibility, Award Information, Application Components, Budget Requirements & Policies, Submission Details, Special Requirements, and Important Notes. The pipeline runs seven parallel Prompt tasks (each emitting a JSON fragment for its block) plus a Consolidation Prompt that renders the final Markdown checklist with strict de-duplication. Mirrors the ui-insight/ProcessMapping rfa-checklist-extraction workflow's eight consolidated sections and placement contract.

data.name: kb-context-lookup
data.query: RFA FOA NOFO eligibility budget cost sharing F&A indirect cost rates allowable unallowable personnel effort submission deadlines compliance requirements Uniform Guidance

_embedded_knowledge_base.title: OMB Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200)
_embedded_knowledge_base.description: Primary regulatory KB for federal funding announcement interpretation. The KnowledgeBaseQueryNode runs against this KB and returns the top-8 chunks matching the query above. Downstream parallel extraction tasks read both the KB chunks (via step_input) and the uploaded RFA PDF (via workflow_documents) into their LLM context. When the operator does not attach a KB in Vandalizer's UI, this step returns empty output gracefully and the parallel tasks fall back to reading just the PDF. The operator can alternatively swap in an agency-specific KB (NSF PAPPG Reference, NIH Grants Policy Statement, DOE Financial Assistance Rules, DOD Research Funding & DFARS) when the RFA's sponsor calls for one.

data.name: extract-opportunity-metadata
data.prompt:
You are extracting the scalar OPPORTUNITY METADATA from a
federal funding announcement (RFA / FOA / NOFO / program
solicitation). You receive the full uploaded document as your
context. Read the entire document — cover page, header,
program description, sponsor information, instructions.

Extract these fields. Quote the document for every value;
never invent. Use null when the document does not state a
value.

- rfa_id: Combined sponsor-prefixed RFA identifier when both
  a sponsor code and opportunity number exist (e.g.,
  "NSF-26-508", "NIH-PA-24-246", "DOE-DE-FOA-0003117"). null
  otherwise.
- rfa_number: The sponsor's announcement number without
  agency prefix (e.g., "26-508", "PA-24-246",
  "DE-FOA-0003117").
- rfa_title: Full title of the funding opportunity, including
  any track or component designation. Required.
- sponsor_name: Full name of the lead sponsoring agency
  (e.g., "National Science Foundation"); never an
  abbreviation. Required.
- program_code: Sponsor's internal program or division code
  (e.g., "NSF/TIP/ITE"); null if not stated.
- announcement_url: Canonical URL of the announcement on the
  sponsor's site; null if not present.
- opportunity_number: Grants.gov or portal opportunity ID
  when distinct from rfa_number; null otherwise.
- cfda_number: CFDA / Assistance Listing number(s); when
  multiple, comma-separate (e.g., "47.070, 47.076").

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these eight keys. No
preamble, no closing commentary, no markdown fences. Example
shape:

{
  "rfa_id": "NSF-26-508",
  "rfa_number": "26-508",
  "rfa_title": "Mid-Scale Research Infrastructure-2 (Mid-scale RI-2)",
  "sponsor_name": "National Science Foundation",
  "program_code": "NSF/TIP",
  "announcement_url": "https://www.nsf.gov/funding/...",
  "opportunity_number": null,
  "cfda_number": "47.083"
}

data.name: extract-dates-and-deadlines
data.prompt:
You are extracting the DATES & DEADLINES block of a federal
funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded document
as your context. Search every section of the document
including the main body, appendices, footnotes, sidebar
callouts.

Extract every unique date or time-bound event in the
announcement. For multi-round solicitations include every
round's LOI, pre-proposal, and full proposal deadlines.

For each date emit an object with these three keys:

- item: The event label exactly as stated in the document
  (e.g., "Letter of Intent Due", "Full Proposal Deadline",
  "Award Notification"). Required.
- date_time: Full date plus any time and timezone as
  published (e.g., "2026-09-15 5:00 PM ET", "2026-10-01",
  "Rolling"). Preserve the sponsor's granularity exactly. Do
  not invent precision. Required.
- notes: Any conditions, round identifiers, or clarifications
  attached to this date (e.g., "Track 1 only", "Optional but
  encouraged"). null when none.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`dates_and_deadlines`, whose value is a JSON array of date
objects sorted chronologically. No preamble, no markdown
fences. Example:

{
  "dates_and_deadlines": [
    {"item": "Letter of Intent Due", "date_time": "2026-08-01 5:00 PM ET", "notes": "Required for full proposal eligibility"},
    {"item": "Full Proposal Deadline", "date_time": "2026-10-15 5:00 PM ET", "notes": null}
  ]
}

data.name: extract-eligible-institutions
data.prompt:
You are extracting the ELIGIBLE INSTITUTIONS subsection of a
federal funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded
document as your context. Read the eligibility section, any
appendix or attached eligibility guidance, and any sponsor
terms-and-conditions referenced inline.

List every distinct institution category the sponsor names.
Put institutional prerequisites (SAM.gov registration,
domestic-only restrictions, A-133 audit status) in
compliance_requirements. Do NOT put PI-level rules here —
those belong to extract-eligible-individuals.

For each institution category emit an object with these four
keys:

- type: Institution category label as stated (e.g.,
  "Institutions of Higher Education", "Nonprofit
  Organizations Other Than Institutions of Higher Education",
  "Small Businesses"). Required.
- subcategory: More specific classification when given (e.g.,
  "R1 research universities", "HBCUs", "EPSCoR-eligible").
  null when the type has no subcategorization.
- examples: Sponsor-supplied examples that illustrate the
  category, as a short comma-separated list. null when the
  announcement gives none.
- compliance_requirements: Registrations, certifications, or
  institutional prerequisites attached to this type. null
  when no institutional compliance terms are attached.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`eligible_institutions`, whose value is a JSON array. MUST
be non-empty — if truly nothing is stated, emit a single
entry with type "Not specified in this document". No
preamble, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-eligible-individuals
data.prompt:
You are extracting the ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS subsection of a
federal funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded
document as your context. Read the eligibility section and
any PI-eligibility appendix.

List every distinct PI / Co-PI / Senior Key Personnel
category the sponsor names. Include citizenship,
career-stage, degree, appointment type, and prior-award
restrictions in criteria or conditions. Limits like "one
nomination per institution" belong to conditions here, not
in Special Requirements.

For each individual category emit an object with these four
keys:

- type: Individual eligibility category (e.g., "Principal
  Investigator", "Early-Career Investigator",
  "Co-Investigator"). Required.
- criteria: Qualifying criteria (degree, career stage,
  appointment type, citizenship); null when none.
- compliance_requirements: ORCID, mentoring plans, or other
  PI compliance items; null when none.
- conditions: Restrictions, limits, or preferences (e.g.,
  "One nomination per institution", "Not eligible if prior
  RFA-awarded"); null when none.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`eligible_individuals`, whose value is a JSON array. MUST be
non-empty — if truly nothing is stated, emit a single entry
with type "Not specified in this document". No preamble, no
markdown fences.

data.name: extract-award-information
data.prompt:
You are extracting the AWARD INFORMATION block of a federal
funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded document
as your context. Read the award-information section, program
description, and any appendix that states funding amounts.

This block is the SOLE location for primary award parameters
in the final deliverable — do NOT capture detailed financial
rules (those belong to extract-budget-requirements).

Extract these four fields:

- award_duration: Anticipated duration as stated (e.g.,
  "3 years", "Up to 5 years with option for 2-year
  extension"). Required.
- amount_per_award: Per-award amount including whether the
  figure is total-costs or direct-costs and any restrictions
  bundled into the headline number (e.g., "$500,000 total
  costs including indirect", "$250,000 direct costs per
  year"). Preserve the sponsor's exact formatting (dollar
  sign, commas, basis annotation). Required.
- number_of_awards: Anticipated count as stated (e.g.,
  "10-15", "Subject to availability of funds"). null only
  when truly absent.
- anticipated_award_date: As stated; ISO YYYY-MM-DD when
  given, otherwise free text (e.g., "Spring 2027"). null
  when absent.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these four keys. No
preamble, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-application-components
data.prompt:
You are extracting the APPLICATION COMPONENTS, SUBMISSION
DETAILS, and SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS blocks of a federal
funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded document
as your context. Read every section that describes what to
submit and how to submit it.

Page limits, font and margin rules, template names, and
naming conventions live on the INDIVIDUAL component (in
special_requirements for that component). Submission
mechanics — portal, file format, upload method — live in
submission_details, NOT on individual components.

Extract these four fields:

- required_components: JSON array of {name, description,
  special_requirements} objects, one per required proposal
  component. MUST be non-empty.
  - name: Component name as stated (e.g., "Project
    Description", "Biographical Sketch", "Data Management
    Plan"). Required.
  - description: What the component must contain, in the
    sponsor's own terms. Required.
  - special_requirements: Page limits, font/margin rules,
    template requirements, or naming conventions specific to
    this component. null when none.
- optional_components: Same item shape as
  required_components; empty array when none.
- submission_details: A single coherent paragraph covering
  submission method / portal, technical and file-format
  requirements, file-naming conventions, and collaboration
  rules. null only when the announcement contains no
  submission guidance at all.
- special_requirements: JSON array of strings — unique RFA
  aspects that do not fit into any other section (conference
  travel obligations, data-sharing commitments beyond federal
  defaults, workshop participation). Empty array when none.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these four keys. No
preamble, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-budget-requirements
data.prompt:
You are extracting the BUDGET REQUIREMENTS & POLICIES block
of a federal funding announcement. You receive the full
uploaded document as your context. Read every section that
states budget rules, cost principles, and personnel effort
requirements.

This block is the SOLE location for detailed financial rules
in the final deliverable — do NOT restate award amount or
duration here (those belong to extract-award-information).

Extract these eight fields. Quote the sponsor's language
verbatim for cost-sharing status (when not "Not Specified"),
salary caps, and unallowable-cost categories.

CRITICAL — descriptive fields must be FLAT STRINGS, not
nested objects. The fields `funding_limits`,
`cost_sharing_details`, `fa_policy`, `personnel_effort`, and
`other_considerations` MUST be emitted as single
natural-language strings (or null). Do NOT emit them as
nested JSON objects with sub-keys — the downstream
Consolidation step renders them verbatim into Markdown, and
nested JSON appears as literal `{...}` in the final
deliverable, which is unreadable. Describe each field as a
short paragraph or comma-joined clause.

Example of WRONG output for cost_sharing_details:
  {"type": ["cash", "in-kind"], "rate": "≥100% of award",
   "documentation": "Matching Fund Verification Letter"}
Example of CORRECT output for cost_sharing_details:
  "Cash and in-kind, matching contributions equal to or
   greater than the FFAR funding request (≥100% of the FFAR
   award), with at least 50% of matching funds in cash;
   documented via Matching Fund Verification Letter(s); must
   come from non–U.S. Federal entities."

- funding_limits: STRING. Program-wide or per-year caps and
  category-specific limits not already covered by
  amount_per_award. null when absent.
- cost_sharing_status: one of "Required", "Voluntary",
  "Prohibited", "Not Specified". Required.
- cost_sharing_details: STRING (single natural-language
  paragraph). Type (cash / in-kind / third-party), rate,
  calculation basis, documentation, source restrictions —
  all concatenated into one readable sentence or short
  paragraph. null when status is "Prohibited" or "Not
  Specified".
- fa_policy: STRING (single natural-language paragraph).
  F&A / indirect cost policy — rate, base (MTDC / TDC / S&W),
  excluded categories, documentation — concatenated into one
  readable description. null when absent.
- allowable_costs: JSON array of CATEGORY-LABEL STRINGS the
  sponsor EXPLICITLY enumerates as allowable. Empty array
  when the announcement simply defers to federal defaults.
- unallowable_costs: JSON array of CATEGORY-LABEL STRINGS
  the sponsor EXPLICITLY enumerates as unallowable. Empty
  array when none.
- personnel_effort: STRING. PI / key-personnel effort floor
  or ceiling, salary caps, student / postdoc support,
  consultant limits. null when absent.
- other_considerations: STRING (single natural-language
  paragraph). Pre-award costs, program income, budget
  revisions, sponsor-specific budget forms — concatenated
  into one readable description. null when
  absent.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these eight keys. No
preamble, no markdown fences.

data.name: rfa-checklist-consolidation
data.prompt:
You are the consolidation step of the RFA Checklist
Extraction workflow. You receive SEVEN JSON object fragments
from the previous step:

1. Opportunity metadata (rfa_id, rfa_number, rfa_title,
   sponsor_name, program_code, announcement_url,
   opportunity_number, cfda_number)
2. Dates and deadlines (array of {item, date_time, notes})
3. Eligible institutions (array of {type, subcategory,
   examples, compliance_requirements})
4. Eligible individuals (array of {type, criteria,
   compliance_requirements, conditions})
5. Award information (award_duration, amount_per_award,
   number_of_awards, anticipated_award_date)
6. Application components (required_components,
   optional_components, submission_details,
   special_requirements)
7. Budget requirements (funding_limits, cost_sharing_status,
   cost_sharing_details, fa_policy, allowable_costs,
   unallowable_costs, personnel_effort, other_considerations)

Your job is to render a single, well-formatted Markdown
checklist for the sponsored-programs analyst (the
end-user). The deliverable is Markdown — NOT a JSON object
and NOT a JSON code fence. The audience is a research
administrator who will copy this into Word, paste into an
email to the proposal team, or save to a shared folder.

## Required structure (in this exact order)

# RFA Checklist: <rfa_title>

**Sponsor:** <sponsor_name>
**RFA ID / Number:** <rfa_id> / <rfa_number>
**Program Code:** <program_code or "Not specified">
**Announcement URL:** <announcement_url or "Not specified">
**Opportunity Number:** <opportunity_number or "Not specified">
**CFDA Number:** <cfda_number or "Not specified">

---

## DATES & DEADLINES

A Markdown table with these three columns and chronologically
sorted rows:

| Deadline / Event | Date / Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| (item) | (date_time) | (notes or "—") |

---

## ELIGIBILITY

### Eligible Institutions

Render each entry as a bulleted item with the type in
**bold**. Add sub-bullets ONLY for subcategory, examples, and
compliance_requirements WHEN THOSE FIELDS ARE POPULATED in
the fragment. Skip any sub-field that is null. If a category
has NO non-null sub-fields, render just the bold type with
no sub-bullets. Example with all sub-fields populated:

- **Institutions of Higher Education**
  - Subcategory: R1 research universities
  - Examples: NSF EPSCoR-eligible institutions
  - Compliance: SAM.gov registration required

Example with no sub-fields populated:

- **Institutions of Higher Education**

### Eligible Individuals

Same bulleted shape — type in **bold** plus sub-bullets for
criteria, compliance_requirements, conditions WHEN THOSE
FIELDS ARE POPULATED. Skip null sub-fields entirely; do NOT
emit "Criteria: —" placeholder lines. Bold key limitations
like **one nomination per institution** when they appear.

---

## AWARD INFORMATION

This is the **sole location** for award parameters. Render as
a definition-style list:

- **Award Duration:** <award_duration>
- **Amount per Award:** <amount_per_award>
- **Anticipated Number of Awards:** <number_of_awards or "Not specified">
- **Anticipated Award Date:** <anticipated_award_date or "Not specified">

Do NOT include any cost-sharing, F&A, or personnel-effort
information here — that goes in BUDGET REQUIREMENTS &
POLICIES.

---

## APPLICATION COMPONENTS

### Required Components

A Markdown table with these three columns. Always present.

| Component Name | Description / Details | Special Requirements |
|---|---|---|

### Optional Components

Same three-column table. If empty, include a single row:

| Not specified in this document | — | — |

---

## BUDGET REQUIREMENTS & POLICIES

This is the **sole location** for detailed financial rules.
Render as a bulleted list with bold labels. CRITICAL — all
the descriptive fields (`funding_limits`,
`cost_sharing_details`, `fa_policy`, `personnel_effort`,
`other_considerations`) are flat strings emitted by the
extraction step. Render them as flat prose. If a fragment
arrives as a nested JSON object instead of a string,
REWRITE it into natural-language prose before emitting —
do NOT pass through `{"key": "value"}` syntax into the
final Markdown.

- **Funding Limits:** <funding_limits prose, or "Not specified">
- **Cost Sharing:** <cost_sharing_status>
    - When status is "Required" or "Voluntary", include
      cost_sharing_details as a natural-language sub-bullet
      paragraph (NOT as JSON).
- **F&A / Indirect Cost Policy:** <fa_policy prose, or "Not specified">
- **Allowable Costs:** bulleted list of allowable_costs,
  or "Defers to federal defaults" when the array is empty.
- **Unallowable Costs:** bulleted list of unallowable_costs,
  or "None explicitly enumerated" when the array is empty.
- **Personnel Effort:** <personnel_effort prose, or "Not specified">
- **Other Considerations:** <other_considerations prose, or "—">

---

## SUBMISSION DETAILS

Render submission_details as a single coherent paragraph. If
null, state "Not specified in the document."

---

## SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS

Render special_requirements as a bulleted list. If empty,
state "None identified beyond standard federal requirements."

---

## IMPORTANT NOTES

Synthesize 0–5 critical warnings or pitfalls a reviewer would
otherwise miss. Pull from across the seven fragments — not
from the document directly. Render as a bulleted list with
each item starting with a bold lead like **Coordinate with
OSP at least 6 weeks before submission** — explanation
follows. Keep this short. If no critical warnings rise to
this bar, state "No critical reviewer warnings beyond what
appears in the sections above."

---

## Placement contract (enforce as you render)

1. **Award amount and duration appear ONLY in AWARD
   INFORMATION.** Even if the budget fragment mentions them,
   do not restate.
2. **Detailed financial rules appear ONLY in BUDGET
   REQUIREMENTS & POLICIES.** Even if the award-info fragment
   mentions matching or indirect-cost notes, move those rules
   to budget.
3. **Per-component formatting rules (page limits, fonts,
   naming) appear ONLY on the individual component's Special
   Requirements column** in the APPLICATION COMPONENTS
   table. Not in the top-level SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS section.
4. **Submission mechanics (portal, file format, naming)
   appear ONLY in SUBMISSION DETAILS.**

## Formatting rules

- Preserve the sponsor's monetary formatting verbatim
  (`$1,234,567`, `$0.5M`, `30% MTDC`).
- Preserve dates exactly as stated, including time and
  timezone components.
- Use `**bold**` for labels and critical action items; use
  `*italics*` sparingly for warnings.
- Use `—` (em dash) for empty optional fields in tables;
  "Not specified in the document" for empty required fields.
- No JSON. No code fences around the output. No preamble. No
  closing commentary about the rendering. The output is the
  deliverable — render it as if you were writing the document
  directly.

validation_plan.check_description: Verify the Markdown deliverable contains all eight sections in order (Dates & Deadlines, Eligibility, Award Information, Application Components, Budget Requirements & Policies, Submission Details, Special Requirements, Important Notes).
Verify award amount and duration appear only in the Award Information section, and detailed financial rules only in the Budget Requirements & Policies section.
Verify monetary amounts preserve the sponsor's original currency formatting (dollar signs, commas, basis annotation).
Verify both Eligible Institutions and Eligible Individuals subsections are present and non-empty.
